text: The project is titled 'Warranty Software Application To Manage Purchases' and was created by Zack Steel.
The application aims to allow purchasers to scan their receipts and warranties for organization and retrieval.
The application would contain relevant data necessary to qualify for a replacement item under warranty coverage.
The project was launched on Kickstarter and had a funding goal of $7,061.
The funding period for the project was from August 25, 2015, to September 24, 2015.
The project funding was unsuccessful as the goal was not reached by the deadline.
The project was last updated on September 24, 2015.
The project is based in Toronto, Canada.
The project had 0 backers and $0 pledged.
To qualify for a replacement item as part of warranty coverage, a person needs to provide specific data.

Necessary items for warranty include the actual receipt containing the serial number of the product, date of purchase, store ID, method of payment, universal price code, item identification number, and transaction number.
The receipt is the most important requirement for warranty redemption of a purchased item.
Manufacturers or suppliers may want to diagnose issues via the internet or request that the purchaser run various tests before providing a replacement item.
Some companies require the old or original product to be sent back before a new or replacement product is given to the customer.
Certain companies send packing slips to be affixed to the box for the item to be returned.
Depending on the purchased product, some companies may only want the electrical cord or plug to be sent in by mail.

The manufacturer may only request compliance with smart recycling practices that adhere to municipal and federal environmental standards for certain items, such as printers, fax machines, or old scanners.
Customers should note the date and time of each telephone call when expressing a complaint about their purchased product.
Providing details of telephone calls demonstrates the customer's effort to follow a reasonable plan to obtain assistance with their product.
Customers may not always receive a new product; they could receive a refurbished item instead.
At the time of purchase, customers can usually buy an extended warranty for their product.
Many credit card companies provide an additional year of product/service coverage, in addition to the initial year of warranty coverage offered by the manufacturer.
Customers should contact their credit card company directly to find out details about the unique warranty option coverage provided under their credit card member's policy.
The Warranty Software Application may include a special feature that notifies users 30, 60, or 90 days before their warranty expires.
The Warranty Software Application may include a feature that notifies users 30, 60, or 90 days before their warranty or extended warranty expiration date.
Vendors, stores, and manufacturers can sell extended warranties directly through the Warranty Application.
The application would source from participating vendors when the product manufacturer is identified on the receipt.
The Warranty Application could provide opportunities for unlimited revenue for each extended warranty sold through the application.
Risks include competitors producing a similar Warranty Application before it can be developed and submitted to the marketplace.
Challenges include fees for items such as a patent and a Proof of Concept demonstration.
Costs for registration of a trademark and copyright for the concept and content are also challenges.
